title: EHS Manager
description: Role Overview We are seeking an EHS Manager to join our manufacturing site in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. This role will be responsible for leading and continuously improving Environmental Compliance, Process Safety, and Occupational Health & Safety activities at the site while ensuring alignment with Huntsman's global EHS standards and Zero Harm culture. The successful candidate will also be an active member of Huntsman's wider EHS network, working closely with global subject matter experts and the EHS Center of Excellence. We are looking for a confident, influential, and independent EHS leader who is able to challenge the status quo, drive a strong safety culture, and effectively engage stakeholders across all levels of the organization. The ideal candidate is a hands-on professional who combines technical EHS expertise with excellent communication skills and the ability to positively influence site leadership and operational teams. Do you think you’re the right fit for this opportunity? Apply today! Role Responsibilities As a EHS Manager, you will be responsible for: Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of the site's EHS Management System, ensuring compliance with company standards and applicable legal requirements. Act as the site's primary EHS leader and focal point for Environmental, Health, Safety, and Process Safety matters. Ensure compliance with environmental, occupational safety, and process safety regulations, maintaining readiness for regulatory inspections and audits. Drive the implementation of Huntsman's Zero Harm strategy and strengthen the site's safety culture through visible leadership and employee engagement. Lead Process Hazard Analyses (PHA), risk assessments, and hazard identification activities, ensuring effective mitigation and closure of actions. Support key process safety programs, including Management of Change (MOC), Pre-Startup Safety Reviews (PSSR), and safe work practices. Lead incident and near-miss investigations, ensuring robust root cause analysis, implementation of corrective actions, and sharing of lessons learned. Oversee critical safety programs including Permit to Work, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), contractor safety, confined space entry, work at height, and chemical handling controls. Monitor environmental performance and ensure compliance with reporting, waste management, emissions, and pollution prevention requirements. Deliver EHS training, coaching, and awareness programs to employees and contractors to reinforce accountability and safe behaviors. Prepare and communicate EHS performance reports, compliance updates, key risks, and action plans to site leadership and relevant stakeholders. Experience And Competencies We are looking for experienced candidates with hands-on EHS experience What We Are Looking For Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety, or a related discipline. 5–10 years of EHS experience within chemical, petrochemical, oil & gas, or other high-hazard manufacturing environments. Fluent English required; Arabic language skills are preferred Strong knowledge of EHS, Process Safety, Risk Management, and Environmental Compliance. Proven experience driving safety culture, EHS programs, and continuous improvement initiatives. Experience conducting risk assessments, incident investigations, and root cause analysis Strong influencing, stakeholder management, and communication skills. Ability to operate independently in a standalone EHS leadership role. OSHA, NEBOSH, IOSH, or an equivalent internationally recognized EHS certification. Experience with Process Hazard Analysis (PHA), Management of Change (MOC), and Process Safety Management (PSM) is preferred. Saudi Arabian nationals are preferred What next? If you would like to join an innovative, collaborative and multicultural team, please apply now. Your application will be forwarded to a Talent Acquisition Partner, who will strive to get back to you as soon as they can. We understand that applying for a new job is a big decision and we will work hard to keep you updated and support you along the way. About Us At Huntsman, we pride ourselves on being a people-oriented organization. Our family-like atmosphere is cultivated by our diverse groups of team members around the world. We welcome the talent, experience and fresh ideas that employees at all stages of their careers, from interns to seasoned professionals, bring to Huntsman. In return, we offer you the opportunity to become an integral part of a dynamic, industry-leading company, where safety and ethics always come first.

Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and diligence. Strong communication and presentation skills. Advanced proficiency in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word), SharePoint, and Power BI. Knowledge of Safety Management Information Systems (SMIS) is an advantage.

title: Field Security Advisor
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role We have created a new standard in cyber extortion incident response and are expanding our Cyber Readiness & Advisory Services team to continue evolving the retained client experience. We are looking for a Field Security Advisor to help us develop and deliver valuable content, tabletop exercises, and training workshops to our enterprise customers. In this role, you will work closely with our Customer Success team and Field CISO organization to help Global 2000 customers prepare executive, technical, finance, legal, and operational teams for the realities of handling a cyber extortion incident and improving organizational resiliency. Coveware is a fully distributed company with employees across multiple geographies. This is a remote role with global time zone flexibility. Design and facilitate tabletop exercises that reflect realistic cyber extortion conditions, operational disruption, ambiguous early facts, and executive decision points. Curate and continuously improve customer-facing content, including playbooks, decision frameworks, readiness checklists, and workshop materials, keeping deliverables aligned to current ransomware/extortion patterns. Conduct research and forensic data analysis to support advisory deliverables and customer insights, including synthesizing lessons learned from case trends and interpreting forensic outputs/artifacts (as available) into clear, actionable readiness recommendations. Support the customer lifecycle as needed, including customer due diligence requests, RFP/RFI questionnaires, and review of contracts/security exhibits in partnership with internal stakeholders. Collaborate internally with case management, SMEs, and other stakeholders to ensure readiness guidance stays grounded in real-world incident behavior and recovery constraints. Technologies You'll Work With Incident Response / Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) tools and methodologies Security Operations platforms and processes Cybersecurity advisory and consulting frameworks MITRE ATT&CK NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) CIS Controls Forensic analysis tools and artifacts Ransomware and cyber extortion readiness frameworks What You'll Bring 7+ years of experience in information security/cybersecurity, with depth in one or more of: Incident response / DFIR Security operations Cyber risk / security advisory / consulting 3+ years of customer-facing experience supporting B2B enterprise customers in advisory, incident readiness, cybersecurity, technology, or forensics-related services. Foundational knowledge of application, identity, cloud and network security concepts, and incident response best practices, ideally in a Global 2000 enterprise environment. Demonstrated experience presenting in a consultative manner to enterprise leadership and facilitating educational workshops and tabletop exercises. Ability to communicate complex topics clearly and authoritatively to diverse audiences, orally and in writing. Willingness and ability to travel for customer meetings, workshops, and events on occasion. Comfortable leading discussions with enterprise stakeholders across both technical and executive teams. Consultative/advisory mindset with structured problem framing, strong facilitation skills, crisp communication, and defensible recommendations. Strong listening skills with excellent written and verbal communication skills and willingness to deliver hard truths when needed to surface gaps and drive improvement. Strong, structured writing skills with experience producing executive-ready, evidence-based deliverables, translating complex inputs into clear narratives, prioritized recommendations, and defensible documentation. Bonus Skills One or more information security certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CCSP, GCIH, GCFE, GCFA). Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Experience translating forensic findings and incident learnings into executive-ready narratives and prioritized readiness actions. Familiarity with frameworks/standards such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF and CIS Controls and how to apply them pragmatically to cyber defense and recovery. Experience collaborating with teammates to stay current on the threat landscape and continuously improve customer-facing materials. title: Shift Operator
description: A Snapshot of your day Your day involves monitoring and controlling gas turbine operations in real time through DCS systems, conducting routine equipment inspections, and ensuring safe, efficient, and reliable power generation across the Khormala Power Plant. You play a key role in minimizing downtime by responding to operational needs, adhering to strict HSE standards, and maintaining the continuous performance of critical plant equipment. How You’ll Make An Impact Monitor and control gas turbine generators, auxiliary systems, and plant equipment through DCS to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. Respond to alarms, investigate system abnormalities, and take corrective or emergency actions to maintain operational continuity. Conduct routine equipment inspections, identify faults or abnormalities, and support troubleshooting and maintenance activities. Safely isolate equipment and implement Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures while verifying plant readiness following maintenance work. Maintain full compliance with HSE standards and environmental regulations through safety inspections, hazard identification, incident reporting, and participation in safety programs. What You Bring Technical Diploma or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, Electrical, Control & Instrumentation Engineering, with 3-5 years of experience in power plant operations, preferably within gas turbine or combined cycle power plants. DCS Operator Certification and a recognized Health & Safety certification such as OSHA, NEBOSH, or equivalent. Strong expertise in Distributed Control Systems (DCS), gas turbine technology, auxiliary equipment, and Balance of Plant (BOP) systems. Proven knowledge of safety procedures including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), hazard identification, risk assessment, and emergency response protocols. Excellent troubleshooting, root cause analysis, technical documentation, shift reporting, communication, and teamwork skills.
